verses.1: And he made it white in the morning. He anointed its branches and leaves with oil. Then he blessed it, and then he went away. And Laban returned to his place.
verses.2: And Jacob went his way, but the angels of God met him on his path.
verses.3: And Yaakov said, “When he saw that place was a place of God’s presence, he called that place “Machanayim”.
verses.4: And Jacob sent his servants before him to their brother Esau, to the land of Seir.
verses.5: And he commanded them, “Say to your Lord, ‘As this servant of yours, Jacob, said: I am old and feeble; yet I still remain here until now.’”
verses.6: And I will have sheep, goats, servants, and women, and I will send them to please you.
verses.7: And the magicians returned to Jacob and said, “We have come to your brother Esau. I will go and call for you. Four thousand men will go with me.”
verses.8: And Jacob was very afraid. He took his people, along with the livestock, and went away to two separate campsites.
verses.9: And he said, “If Esau comes to the other tent and attacks it, then the remaining tent will be saved.”
verses.10: And Jacob said, “Lord of my father Abraham and Lord of my father Isaac, may the Lord say to me, ‘Return to your land and to your home.’”
verses.11: I am overwhelmed by all your kindnesses and all the truth you have done for your servants. In my youth, I crossed this Jordan River. Now, I am one of two camps here.
verses.12: Save me from my brother’s hand, from the hand of Esau. I fear him too much; he will come and harm me. Please protect me from his actions.
verses.13: And you said, “It is good to be with you.” And I have placed your seed like the waves of the sea, which cannot be measured.
verses.14: And he lay there that night. He took some food from what was in his hand, and gave it to his brother Esau.
verses.15: Thirty oxen, and thirty sheeps; thirty doves, and thirty sheep.
verses.16: They had many children; among them were thirty daughters, forty sons, twelve grandsons, and twenty grandsons.
verses.17: And he gave his servants a single reed. He said to them, “Go ahead and stand in front of me. Then place the wood between the two reeds.”
verses.18: And he commanded the first one, “When Esau meets you, he will ask you, ‘Who are you? To whom are you going?’”
verses.19: And you said, “Let Jacob serve you as a gift from Me. It’s a gift to the Lord, so that He may do what He wants.” And behold, he is also among our friends.
verses.20: And he also commanded the second and the third, and all those who followed the traditions, to say this same words to Isaac when they found him.
verses.21: And you said, “Look, your servant Jacob will follow us. As it is written, ‘His face will be covered with ashes when he goes before us.’ After that, I will see his face again.”
verses.22: And the blood passed over his face. And he lay there in that night, in the camp.
verses.23: And in the night, he got up. He took with him two of his wives, two of his daughters, and eleven of his children. Then he crossed over the river Yabok.
verses.24: And he took them across the river, and he crossed over those who were with him.
verses.25: And Jacob was left alone. No one stayed with him until they reached the black rock.
verses.26: And he saw that he could not do it. His foot was trapped, and Jacob’s foot became stuck in the mud along with him.
verses.27: And he said, “Send me up.” But the blacksmith replied, “I will not send you up, unless you bless me first.”
verses.28: And he said to him, “What is your name?” And he replied, “Yaakov.”
verses.29: And he said, “Do not say, ‘Your name will be remembered.’ For it shall be said, ‘Israel has indeed been made holy by God and by men.’”
verses.30: And Jacob asked for his name. He said, “Please tell me your name.” Then he blessed him there.
verses.31: And Yaakov called the name of that place “Pheni’el,” because I saw God’s face. My soul was saved.
verses.32: And the sun shone upon him as it passed over Penuel; and he was illuminated by its light.
verses.33: Therefore, the children of Israel shall not eat the blood of a female animal that is slaughtered on the day before today. For Jacob’s hand touched the blood of the female animal during that time.
